summary.text: A 12-year-old male with osteosarcoma of the femur diagnosed in August 2012 received neoadjuvant chemotherapy with adriamycin, cisplatin, ifosfamide and methotrexate, femur removal in December 2012 and further chemotherapy. During the last cycle in June 2013, hypertransaminasemia was detected, with ALT 456 U/L, and he had no clinical findings.

Further tests showed worsening AST and ALT, and the serologic panel showed acute HBV infection with D genotype, despite correct vaccination and a negative HBsAg at presurgical screening. Because of the risk of fulminant hepatitis, off-label tenofovir 245 mg once a day was started. After 30 days HBV-DNA had decreased, and transaminases and coagulation parameters had normalized.

After 5 months of TDF treatment he developed normoglycemic glycosuria, hypophosphatemia and proteinuria, leading to a diagnosis of Fanconi syndrome associated with TDF therapy. TDF was withdrawn with a switch to entecavir; tubulopathy resolved after 2 months, and a complete HBs seroconversion occurred after 6 months.

Nucleoside analogue therapy was stopped 18 months after seroconversion, and persistence of the HBs seroconversion was confirmed 2 years after the end of treatment. The oncological disease is currently in remission.
